exact_claim: The reference manuscript's thm:main asserts that, for n>=1, the normal projective n-dimensional base of a projective surjective holomorphic morphism with connected fibers from a compact 2n-dimensional IHS Kahler manifold is P^n_C, when every component of every fiber has dimension n and is Lagrangian. The full theorem is not established by the old local clearing certificate.
hypotheses: X is compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic and Kahler, of complex dimension 2n, n>=1.
f:X->B is projective and surjective with connected fibers; projectivity is relative ampleness.
B is a normal projective variety of complex dimension n.
Every irreducible component of every fiber has dimension n and the symplectic form restricts to zero on its smooth locus.
The original X is consequently projective; nearby fixed-class deformations used in the proof may be nonprojective Kahler.
The theorem does not assume B smooth, a known deformation type, or an extra b2 bound; its proof deduces b2>=4 and must cover rank four separately.
The final quotient-elimination dependency additionally requires a finite surjective cover A->B from an n-dimensional abelian variety and uses the original projective fibration.
result_class: A full global geometric manuscript theorem with explicitly identified dependencies beyond the inherited conditional local algebra; bounded scope review, not an end-to-end proof or refutation.
supported_scope: The old claim accurately records the reference theorem's projective, connected-fiber, equidimensional Lagrangian scope.
Relative projectivity over a projective base with Kahler source makes the original X projective; the theorem is not an unrestricted proper-Kahler assertion.
The source reduces the theorem to smoothness of B and identifies a conditional final application of Hwang's smooth-base theorem.
The Euler target is the ordinary Euler characteristic of the coarse minimal stratum, retaining full stabilizers rather than weighted orbifold Euler characteristic.
The source explicitly separates the b2>=5, rank-four isotrivial and rank-four varying cases.
The absence of codimension-one multiple fibers is stated as a consequence after B=P^n, not a hypothesis used to assert the base theorem.
unsupported_scope: Derivation of B=P^n from a local Cartier clearing witness or from projective-space cohomology alone.
Independent verification of the residual tensor classification, compatible global stratum and ordinary Euler obstruction.
Replacement of the simultaneous fixed-target family on the full nearby e-Hodge locus by a deformation with varying targets or one degenerate-twistor line.
Automatic existence of the second system, actual parallel-transport operators or finite abelian cover from abstract lattice identities alone.
Elimination of nonidentity quotient stabilizers merely from rational smoothness or existence of a finite cover.
Verification or refutation of the entire manuscript, or original novelty credit for the Argus draft.
open_obligations: Establish the residual cotangent tensor classification and compatible minimum stratum/product groupoids, then use arbitrary ordinary coefficient base change, a full truncated End quotient with nilpotent kernel and full-stabilizer character extraction to prove chi_top(S0)=0.

Establish a simultaneous proper map to B x D on the entire nearby e-Hodge locus, with connected Lagrangian fibers and unchanged marked class e, rather than only generated bundles with possibly varying Stein targets.

Derive positive ordinary Euler characteristic of the same minimal stratum in all three cases: b2>=5, rank-four isotrivial and rank-four varying, with the exact period-continuation or two-system hypotheses.

Construct an actual nearby projective model carrying two nef isotropic systems with all positive combinations Kahler, using the stated companion and actual-monodromy inputs, and prove finite surjectivity to the unchanged B on its smooth abelian fibers.

Under quotient singularities and that abelian cover, prove the representable finite-flat lifts, simultaneous nonvanishing translation field and labelled-relation maximality argument eliminate every nonidentity stabilizer; only then apply the smooth-base theorem.

source_checks.finding: The reference author/date, full theorem hypotheses, all-dimension/deformation-type scope, companion inputs and two-stage smoothness strategy were checked.
The original X is projective, the pullback class is nonzero nef isotropic, b2>=4 is deduced, and the unrestricted companion semiampleness theorem is an explicit additional input.
Finite local covers, rational smoothness and residual SL/Sp tensor blocks are separate geometric and representation-theoretic obligations, not consequences of scalar clearing.
The nonquotient case requires a global normal projective stratum, marked product groupoids, full stabilizers, compatible tensor fixed parts and ordinary supported descent.

The Euler obstruction uses a full truncated End quotient with nilpotent kernel and three dual coefficient tests recovering the trivial representation of every full stabilizer, followed by ordinary coarse de Rham Euler comparison.

The fixed target on the full nearby Hodge locus is an extra assertion. Positive Euler characteristic in rank at least five uses irreducibility of a rank-at-least-three null cone, explicitly unavailable in rank four.
The rank-four branches have distinct zero-variation and varying-two-system hypotheses; the varying argument requires geometric full-monodromy tensor fixed parts.

Both fibrations must occur on the same actual nearby projective model, with the original base retained and finite abelian-fiber restrictions. Integral isometries are not conflated with actual family parallel transports.
